Honestly, Excel seems easier to me, with the caveat that Excel serves two purposes.

The "I need some place to organize tabular data" use case is so different that I'm not considering it for the rest of this.

Claude itself isn't limited to Excel; it can use pandas and the much, much improved plotting tools compared to Excel. I'm an OpenAI guy myself and used codecs to have it make me ggplot2 graphs, but then I forgot to specify it and it just used straight-up Python — I think it actually generated them as SVG files. Regular Excel doesn't even compare there; not only can ggplot2 make many additional types of graphs, but SVG plotting, Python, and pandas can make literally any chart you want, including things like polar-coordinate charts.

I did my first claude slides presentation. I don't see myself voluntarily loading up PowerPoint again.

Now it'll be harder to do the same for word and harder still for excel, but word is doable, and claude can build one off tools better than excel can, so I definitely think that MS should be wary.

children.text: Congratulations you just invented Github Flavored Markdown or, like, Excel 1998 spreadsheet embed inside Word 1998

I have a different approach to the industry when it comes to work documents.

I'm building https://smalldocs.org / https://github.com/espressoplease/smalldocs. My take is that the siloed approach of previous document formats is now redundant. The document formats were isolated because we needed heavy tools for humans to do the work. Now we need lightweight javascript predominately for rending as agents do the work, so document formats can be blended.

This means SmallDocs allows an agent to put together a document (the underlying format is markdown with rich custom rendering on top) with text, diagrams, a multi tab spreadsheet, charts, code, slides, etc.

Some example SmallDocs:

* AlphaFold 3: capabilities, evidence and operational limits (diagram, spreadsheets, charts, code, math): https://smalldocs.org/s/k9BtoviHg1eMsWzrSDBVZM#k=v0oIAbORXDj...

* Profitable growth can run out of cash (slides, spreadsheet, charts): https://smalldocs.org/s/nfCr0EEduLQwZAr0_v9ZR2#k=tv_BjigEYwt...

children.author: 2001zhaozhao
children.text:
The interesting part is that anyone can create these productivity apps now; all that Anthropic has that others don't is the model moat. Namely, people can access models cheaper in Claude.ai compared to paying API prices for other people's tools, and Anthropic's tools come bundled with the discounted model access itself.

In other words they're able to create an entire ecosystem around this cost advantage and there's very little others (without their own models with higher cost-performance than public ones) can do about it.
